rv.q: ...never quite fulfils its potential, offering reflections and textures without cohesion.
Serdar Biliş reaches back over two millennia to adapt Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis and makes it speak, pointedly, uncomfortably, insistently to us, right here, right now.
But rather than disrupting flow, these moments effectively imbue the play’s classical exchanges with a modern sense of jeopardy and desperation.

cn.t: An earnest but ill-conceived production that intersperses Euripides' tragedy with contemporary testimonials about violence, creating a disjointed experience that lacks cohesion despite timely political resonance and strong performances.
